first.rationale: I currently favor simplifying onboarding because completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, while the inherited evidence suggests onboarding changes can improve both completion and time-to-value. I would verify the onboarding and activation records, and compare them with the promotional-pricing record given the competitor threat. Run a guarded test with qualified-revenue, retention, and lead-quality safeguards rather than optimizing completion alone; promotional pricing remains a plausible alternative if verification shows the competitor response is materially stronger.

final.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding-shortening experiment this week. It directly addresses the 4% completion decline and has the strongest verified sustainable-value signal: completion improved 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%. Activation messaging is a credible fallback, but onboarding is the more upstream intervention. Exclude promotional pricing because its 18% qualified-revenue lift was offset by a 12% retention decline at renewal. Evaluate activation, completion, time-to-value, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention, with retention and revenue guardrails to avoid optimizing completion at the expense of durable growth.
